Laura / Karthik — draft attached. Key highlights below; see attached PDF and workbook for full line-item math.

SUMMARY (three customer-facing commercial options)

Option A — Pay-as-you-go (Hosted API)
- Definition: billable token = input + output tokens counted at generation time.
- Pricing (list): $0.00095 per input token; $0.00105 per output token.
- No minimum commit; ideal for Proof-of-Concept.
- Notes: No true-up; no committed discounts. Regional uplift applies to EU:+8%.

Option B — Committed Bucket (12-mo) — Recommended for production
- Structure: Customer commits to a monthly baseline (example: 50M tokens/month) for 12 months; unused baseline does not roll forward.
- Pricing (example band for 50M tpm): effective blended rate $0.00065 per token for up to 100% of committed usage.
- Overage: usage between 100%–150% charged at blended overage rate = $0.00095 per token. Usage beyond 150% triggers an automatic burst pool billing at $0.00160 per token and a monthly true-up.
- Graceband: first 3 months allow up to +/-30% usage variance with no true-up.
- Soft credits: one-time 10% onboarding credit applied to first invoice (non-refundable).

Option C — Hybrid: Baseline commit + Burst Pool (best for spiky workloads)
- Structure: Lower baseline (e.g., 30M tpm) + pooled burst capacity (pre-purchased or on-demand).
- Pricing: baseline blended $0.00058/token; burst pool rate (pre-purchased) $0.0009/token; on-demand burst $0.0015/token.
- True-up: monthly for baseline; burst pool is consumed before on-demand billing.

Negotiation levers (what sales can move):
- Compression / quantization suggestions (model-dependent) — can reduce effective tokens by ~8–15% on embeddings/heavy prompt use-cases.
- Commit length: 24-month term lowers baseline blended rate by additional 12%.
- Billing cadence: monthly vs quarterly true-up — quarterly reduces admin friction but increases cash exposure.
- Marketplace listing fees: if going via a cloud marketplace, add 6–9% fee to list prices.

Legal/Finance notes for Karthik:
- Refundability: onboarding credits are non-refundable; recommend non-refundable language to avoid billing complexity.
- Overage cap: proposed cap is automatic burst pricing beyond 150% to protect capacity — need legal to confirm auto-billing language.
- SLA credits: separate from token billing; reference standard SLA doc.

Attached: Redwood_Pricing_Playbook_QA.pdf (one-pager + appendix), MVP_SKU_and_Appendix.xlsx (workbook with toggles and example scenarios).

If this looks good I can redact the internal negotiation guidance and send to Sarah with the workbook.

Marissa Cole
